title: Operando Optical Microscopy of Lithium Metal Anodes for High-energy-density Batteries
content: Lithium (Li) metal anodes are a promising candidate to replace graphite, which is the active material that is currently used in most state-of-the-art Li-ion batteries. Compared to graphite, Li metal anodes have the potential to significantly increase energy density, owing to their higher specific capacity. However, despite the tremendous interest in replacing graphite with metallic Li, there remain several fundamental challenges that must be addressed to enable the use of a reversible Li metal anode in a rechargeable battery [1]. In particular, Li metal anodes suffer from limited interfacial stability against both liquid and solid-state electrolytes, and are prone to formation of non-planar morphologies during plating and stripping, including dendrites and pits along the surface.
